requirements.title: Database is not reachable from the internet
requirements.description: The database has no public endpoint, lives in subnets without an internet route, and accepts connections only from the application tier.
requirements.source: Interview: data_sensitivity = Customers' personal data; needs_database = Yes, PostgreSQL
requirements.rationale: A publicly reachable database is the most common cause of customer data exposure.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based policies; live check of PubliclyAccessible and security group rules after a real deployment.

requirements.title: Data encrypted at rest
requirements.description: Database storage, server volumes and log storage are encrypted.
requirements.source: Interview: data_sensitivity = Customers' personal data
requirements.rationale: Protects data in snapshots, backups and decommissioned disks.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based policies on storage_encrypted, EBS and S3 encryption settings.

requirements.title: Data encrypted in transit
requirements.description: Users connect over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+); HTTP redirects to HTTPS; database connections require TLS.
requirements.source: Interview: tls = Yes, HTTPS with an ACM certificate
requirements.rationale: Prevents interception of credentials and customer data.

requirements.title: No administrative or database ports exposed to the internet
requirements.description: No security group allows SSH, RDP, database or all-port access from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Administration uses AWS Systems Manager Session Manager.
requirements.source: Interview: admin_access = AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (no open ports)
requirements.rationale: Internet-exposed administrative interfaces are continuously scanned and brute-forced.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based analysis of every ingress rule.

requirements.title: Application servers reachable only through the load balancer
requirements.description: Application security group accepts traffic only from the load balancer security group.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Keeps servers off the internet even if they have public IPs for outbound traffic.

requirements.title: Least-privilege access for workloads
requirements.description: Application servers use a role with only the permissions they need; no administrator policies, wildcard grants or IAM users with access keys.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Limits the blast radius of a compromised server.

requirements.title: Secrets are never stored in configuration
requirements.description: Database credentials are generated and held by AWS Secrets Manager; no credentials appear in Terraform, user data or tags.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Terraform state and plan files are widely readable and long-lived.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based attribute policy plus supplementary credential pattern scan.

requirements.title: Server metadata service hardened
requirements.description: Instances require IMDSv2 session tokens.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Mitigates SSRF-based theft of instance credentials.

requirements.title: Log storage is private and tamper-resistant
requirements.description: The log bucket blocks all public access, is encrypted and versioned.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Logs often contain sensitive data and are evidence during incidents.

requirements.title: Audit trail of infrastructure changes
requirements.description: A multi-region CloudTrail trail with log file validation records every AWS API call.
requirements.source: Interview: audit_logging = Yes, record an audit trail; compliance = None that I know of
requirements.rationale: Answers who changed what, and when.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based CloudTrail policy; live trail status after a real deployment.

requirements.title: Network and request logging
requirements.description: VPC flow logs and load balancer access logs are delivered to the private log bucket.
requirements.source: Interview: audit_logging = Yes, record an audit trail; environment = Production
requirements.rationale: Needed to investigate incidents and abuse.

requirements.title: Application keeps running when a server fails
requirements.description: An auto scaling group with load balancer health checks keeps at least 2 instance(s) running across two availability zones.
requirements.source: Interview: availability = Short outages (minutes to an hour) are acceptable; environment = Production
requirements.rationale: Servers fail; replacement must be automatic.

requirements.title: Automated database backups retained ≥ 7 day(s)
requirements.description: Point-in-time recovery is available for at least 7 day(s).
requirements.source: Interview: recovery_window = 7 days; compliance = None that I know of
requirements.rationale: Recovers from data corruption and accidental deletion.

requirements.title: Production data protected from accidental deletion
requirements.description: Deletion protection is enabled and a final snapshot is taken if the database is ever deleted.
requirements.source: Interview: environment = Production
requirements.rationale: A single mistaken command must not destroy customer data.

requirements.title: Capacity scales with traffic
requirements.description: Target-tracking auto scaling adds servers when average CPU exceeds 60%.
requirements.source: Interview: traffic = Moderate; traffic_pattern = Fairly steady, day and night
requirements.rationale: The original request mentioned handling increasing traffic.

requirements.title: Estimated monthly cost within $400
requirements.description: The selected architecture's estimated monthly cost does not exceed the budget. Security controls are never removed to meet it.
requirements.source: Interview: budget = $400 / month
requirements.rationale: Stated monthly budget.
requirements.verification_method: Cost model estimate (approximate; not a billing guarantee).

requirements.title: Uploaded files are private and encrypted
requirements.description: User files live in a dedicated S3 bucket that blocks all public access, is encrypted and versioned, rejects unencrypted connections, and is readable and writable only by the application's role.
requirements.source: Interview: file_uploads = Yes, store files in a private S3 bucket; data_sensitivity = Customers' personal data
requirements.rationale: Misconfigured file buckets are a leading cause of public data leaks.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based S3 and IAM policies; every bucket in the plan is checked.

requirements.title: Logs retained for at least 90 days
requirements.description: Log bucket lifecycle rules and CloudWatch log groups keep logs for at least 90 days before deleting them.
requirements.source: Interview: log_retention = 90 days; compliance = None that I know of
requirements.rationale: Logs are the evidence trail for incident investigations and audits.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based lifecycle expiration and log group retention policy.

requirements.title: Someone is alerted when the service is unhealthy
requirements.description: CloudWatch alarms on load balancer errors and unhealthy servers and database CPU and free storage notify ops@example.com through an encrypted SNS topic.
requirements.source: Interview: ops_team = A developer with some AWS experience; alerting = Yes, send email alerts; alert_email = ops@example.com
requirements.rationale: Problems should reach your team before they reach your customers.
requirements.verification_method: Plan-based check that alarms watch the load balancer and notify a subscribed, encrypted topic.

requirements.title: Resources are tagged for ownership and cost tracking
requirements.description: Every taggable resource carries Project, Environment and ManagedBy tags.
requirements.source: Security-first baseline (always applied)
requirements.rationale: Enables cost allocation and safe cleanup.

assumptions.statement: PostgreSQL 16 on Amazon RDS is the database engine.
assumptions.reason: You indicated a relational database; PostgreSQL is a widely supported default.

assumptions.statement: Application servers run Amazon Linux 2023 on Graviton (arm64) instances and Node.js listens on port 3000 behind the load balancer.
assumptions.reason: Lowest-cost general-purpose option, with the usual default port for your runtime; a placeholder app is installed until you deploy your own.
The minimum for a load balancer and a Multi-AZ-capable database.

assumptions.statement: AWS-managed encryption keys are used (not customer-managed KMS keys).
assumptions.reason: No extra cost or key administration; switch to customer-managed keys if your compliance program requires key control.

assumptions.statement: Terraform state is stored locally for this MVP.
assumptions.reason: Avoids creating a state bucket; not suitable for teams or production.

assumptions.statement: The database starts with 20 GB of storage and grows automatically up to 100 GB.
assumptions.reason: Sized from your first-year data estimate.

assumptions.statement: You will supply an issued ACM certificate ARN for your domain before a real deployment.
assumptions.reason: HTTPS requires a certificate; the simulation uses a placeholder ARN.

unresolved: ACM certificate ARN for the application's domain (required before a real deployment).
Confirm the SNS email subscription: AWS sends a confirmation link to ops@example.com after a real deployment.
